To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multifunctionality of the enzyme has evolved by gene fusion.
the cDNA of the thioesterase (TE) and acyl carrier (ACP) domains of chicken fatty-acid synthase (FAS) was expressed in E.coli using a plasmid containing the PL promoter.

the multifunctionality of the animal fatty acid synthase has evolved from a fusion of component genes, and that the recombinant fatty acid synthase is a useful model for the study of the structure and function relationships of the individual domains of this enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of fatty acid synthesis.
the characterization of the recombinantly expressed acyl carrier protein/thioesterase domain of the multifunctiononal fatty acid synthase of chicken liver.

the elucidation of the mechanism and regulation of fatty acid biosynthesis, the identification of the structural genes for fatty acid biosynthesis enzymes, and the cloning of the genes into vectors for expression in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expressed recombinant protein has a structure and function similar to the native protein.
this recombinant protein is a functional analog of the thioesterase component of fatty acid synthase.
the expressed protein is a functional domain of the multifunction enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cDNA clones for the multifunctional enzyme have been identified and that the recombinant domains of the synthase are active in vitro.
the multifunction enzyme is composed of 2 subunits, each of which is comprised of 7 partial activities and an acyl carrier protein (ACP) domain.
the chicken FAS cDNA clones are useful for studying the structure and function as well as the evolution of the FAS gene and the enzyme itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multifunctionality of fatty acid synthase is not a result of the interaction of multiple enzymes, but is the result of a single polypeptide chain that contains all of the necessary catalytic sites.
the recombinant thiolase domain has the same substrate and kinetic properties as native fatty acid synthases.

we have been able to produce recombinant thioseterase and acyl protein carrier protein domains from fatty acid synthase in E. coli and that they are functional and have the same substrate specificity as the native enzyme.
